description: Milestone 1: Transform Mohist from a deterministic workflow engine into an AI agent with its own LLM. Single issue, fully automatic, Main Agent (LLM orchestrator) + Code Agent (opencode subprocess), no Event Bus, no gate, no workflow.yaml.

tasks.title: Add AI SDK dependencies
tasks.description: Add ai, @ai-sdk/anthropic, and zod to packages/cli. These are the core dependencies for the agent runtime (D3).
acceptanceCriteria: npm install succeeds without errors
npm run build passes
ai and @ai-sdk/anthropic are in package.json dependencies
tasks.notes: Only add dependencies, no code changes. Start with Anthropic as the only bundled provider.

tasks.title: Implement LLM provider resolver
tasks.description: Create agent-runtime/llm.ts with resolveModel(config) that reads model config from ~/.mohist/config.json, detects API key from environment variables (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY), creates AI SDK provider instance, and returns a LanguageModel. Follow opencode's getSDK + getLanguage pattern (simplified). M1 supports only Anthropic and OpenAI as bundled providers.
acceptanceCriteria: resolveModel returns a LanguageModel instance from config.json + env vars
Missing API key throws a clear error message
Missing config.json falls back to env vars only with a sensible default model
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Read config via existing ConfigService/ConfigRepo. The llm config goes under the 'llm' key in config table. Reference: opencode provider.ts lines 1186-1317 (getSDK) and 1343-1368 (getLanguage).

tasks.title: Implement tool system
tasks.description: Create agent-runtime/tool.ts with Tool.define(id, { description, parameters: zodSchema, execute }) and ToolRegistry.register/get/clear. Each tool has a Zod-validated parameters schema and an execute function returning a string result.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool.define creates a tool with validated parameters
ToolRegistry registers and retrieves tools by ID
Invalid parameters return a validation error string to the LLM
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Keep it simple. No truncation, no middleware. The execute function signature: (params: validated) => Promise<string>.

tasks.title: Implement in-memory session manager
tasks.description: Create agent-runtime/session.ts with SessionManager using a Map<sessionId, Session>. Session has: id, issueId, messages (CoreMessage[]), createdAt, closedAt. Methods: create(issueId), appendMessage(sessionId, message), getMessages(sessionId), close(sessionId). Pure in-memory, no SQLite (D8).
acceptanceCriteria: create generates a unique session ID and stores it in memory
appendMessage adds a message to the session's history
getMessages returns the full message history for LLM calls
close marks session as closed
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Use AI SDK's CoreMessage type for messages. ~50 lines total. No SQLite, no persistence (D8). Session data lost on server restart.

tasks.title: Implement LLM tool loop
tasks.description: Create agent-runtime/agent-loop.ts with runAgentLoop(session, tools, model, options). The function uses AI SDK streamText() with maxSteps to implement the tool calling cycle: build messages from session history, resolve tools from ToolRegistry, call streamText with tools, process tool calls (execute tools, feed results back), persist messages to session, and return when LLM produces final text or maxSteps reached.
acceptanceCriteria: LLM loop calls tools and feeds results back automatically
Loop stops when LLM produces final text (no more tool calls)
Loop stops when maxSteps is reached
All messages (including tool results) are appended to session
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: This is the core runtime. Reference: opencode's SessionProcessor.process() and LLM.stream(). The streamText() call should set maxSteps (default 20). Handle tool execution errors by returning error string to LLM.

tasks.title: Implement spawn_agent tool
tasks.description: Create tools/spawn-agent.ts. This tool spawns an opencode subprocess in the issue's worktree directory. Parameters: { agent_type: string, task: string, cwd?: string, timeout?: number }. Implementation: spawn 'opencode agent --local --message <task>' with cwd set to worktree, capture stdout/stderr/exit_code, wait for completion, return formatted result. Reuse spawn logic from existing agent/runner.ts (D2, C7).
acceptanceCriteria: spawn_agent spawns opencode subprocess in the specified cwd
Subprocess stdout and stderr are captured
Timeout (default 30 min) kills subprocess and returns error
Exit code 0 returns success with stdout content
Non-zero exit code returns error with stderr content
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: M1: spawn_agent directly spawns opencode (no child LLM loop). This is a transparent pass-through. M3 will upgrade to child LLM loop, but the tool interface stays the same.

tasks.title: Implement Mohist domain tools
tasks.description: Create three tools: advance_stage (tools/advance-stage.ts) updates issues.stage in SQLite via IssueRepo, add_comment (tools/add-comment.ts) inserts a comment via CommentRepo, and get_issue (tools/get-issue.ts) reads current issue state. All three tools receive a context object with db repos on creation.
acceptanceCriteria: advance_stage updates issue stage in database and returns new stage
add_comment inserts a comment with timestamp and returns success
get_issue returns issue title, body, stage, and number
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: These tools need access to IssueRepo and CommentRepo. Pass a context object (with repos) to each tool's execute function via closure or dependency injection.

tasks.title: Define Code Agent and Main Agent
tasks.description: Create agents/code-agent.ts with CodeAgentDef (agent name, buildPrompt helper). Create agents/main-agent.ts with the Main Agent: system prompt (hardcoded design → implement → done flow), tool set assembly (spawn_agent, advance_stage, add_comment, get_issue), and a run function that creates a session and starts the agent loop.
acceptanceCriteria: Main Agent has a system prompt with role, workflow stages, and tool descriptions
Main Agent assembles its tool set from the four M1 tools
Main Agent run function creates a session and calls runAgentLoop
CodeAgentDef exports name and buildPrompt helper
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: M1: CodeAgentDef is a definition file (prompt template), not an independent LLM loop. Main Agent's system prompt should be a static template string with variable interpolation for issue context.

tasks.title: Wire start endpoint to Main Agent
tasks.description: Modify api/issues.ts POST /:number/start to create a session, prepare tool context (repos, worktree path), and launch the Main Agent agent loop (async, non-blocking). Also modify server/index.ts to remove WorkflowEngine creation and startup — M1 does not need the old engine. The start endpoint should return immediately with session info while the agent loop runs in the background.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/issues/:number/start creates a session and launches Main Agent
Start endpoint returns immediately (does not wait for agent to finish)
Running issue stage is set to 'designing' on start
server/index.ts no longer creates or starts WorkflowEngine
npm run build passes
tasks.notes: The start endpoint becomes fire-and-forget. The agent loop runs as a background async task. Error handling: if the agent loop throws, mark the issue as failed. D12: single issue — return error if an issue is already running.
